newsitem.title: USA: US Housing starts down in March as Midwest slumps.
newsitem.headline: US Housing starts down in March as Midwest slumps.

text.p: Construction starts on new homes and apartments fell in March after a burst of activity during February, when exceptionally mild weather helped builders, the Commerce Department said on Wednesday.
Total starts declined 6.4 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.43 million in March following a revised 10.7 percent surge in February to 1.52 million a year.
March building activity was slightly weaker than forecast by Wall Street analysts who had anticipated starts at a rate of 1.46 million a year.
The falloff in March building was heavily concentrated in the Midwest, where heavy rains and severe flooding pulled construction activity down at the steepest rate in more than three years.

Recent increases in interest rates, which affect not only homebuyers' ability to qualify for mortgages but also builders' costs to initiate projects, may put some constraint on the housing industry in coming months.
The March building rate was down 0.3 percent from a year earlier in March 1996 when they were at a rate of 1.43 million a year.
Previously, the department said February starts had increased 12.2 percent to a rate of 1.53 million a year but it revised that down modestly.

The National Association of Home Builders said on Monday that its index of market activity fell in April by two points to a level of 56. Higher interest rates were slowing down the pace of construction, the builders said, though they added the index was still healthy.

"It definitely looks like builders are worried, not only about the current level of interest rates but also about where rates are headed," said Kent Colton, chief executive officer of the builder's lobby group.

Nonetheless, the economy expanded vigorously throughout the first quarter, creating hundreds of thousands of jobs and bolstering incomes so that analysts said there was little likelihood of a major slowdown in housing markets.

Construction starts on single-family homes fell 8.3 percent in March to a rate of 1.12 million after rising by an identical 8.3 percent in February. Starts on multiple-unit buildings like apartments and condominiums increased 1.3 percent to 308,000 a year following a 21.6 percent jump in February.
Mortage rates rose in March from February. The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said rates for a 30-year loan averaged 7.90 percent in March, up from from 7.65 percent in February.
Rates have since moved above 8 percent in April for a 30-year loan.
Regionally, starts plunged 20.2 percent in the Midwest during March to a rate of 292,000 -- the biggest monthly decline since a 25.8 percent drop in March 1994, the department said.
But Midwest starts had shot up 40.8 percent in February.
Starts also fell during March in the South, the nation's biggest regional housing market, by 7.1 percent to an annual rate of 619,000 after a 13.1 percent incresae in February.

March starts increased 11.5 percent in the Northeast to a rate of 146,000 after a 28 percent fall in February. In the West, March starts rose 2.5 percent to 368,000 a year after a 4.4 percent increase in February.
